newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition calls for SPD compromise on taxes.
newsitem.headline: German coalition calls for SPD compromise on taxes.

text.p: Leaders of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's German coalition government appealed to opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Monday to show willingness to compromise at a crunch tax reform summit.
"Today is a decisive day for conquering unemployment," Peter Hintze, general secretary of Kohl's Christian Democrat Union (CDU) told ZDF public television.

Leaders of Kohl's 14-year-old coalition and the SPD, both stunned by January's rise in unemployment to the highest since 1933, have agreed to parley on tax reforms to try to create the conditions to boost investment and jobs.

Hintze called on the SPD to be ready to hold a constructive dialogue. "If both sides enter the talks without preconditions and are ready to work fairly on reforms, the talks could lead to success," he told ZDF.
Guido Westerwelle, general secretary of junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP), called the meeting "one of the last big chances for politicians to win the battle against unemployment."
The coalition and the SPD will meet at 1400 GMT for initial talks on a two-year package of 30 billion marks ($17.9 billion) in tax cuts crafted by Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
Failed talks could put the tax package through a tortuous parliamentary process, where the SPD could block key elements through its majority in the upper house of parliament.
The centrepiece of the coalition reform proposals are big cuts in personal and corporate taxes to be partly offset by scrapping over 70 tax breaks.

The SPD has signalled willingness to compromise on some elements of the reform but is set against coalition plans to slash the top rate of income tax and abolish tax allowances for anti-social working hours.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097 150 ($ = 1.672 German Marks)
